{"id":"mimid-1wgh.114.16","title":"Decide what a front end does with a pending invite to a call room","design":"Step 3 of bead mimid-1wgh.130, split out because it is a decision and
not the plumbing. Steps 1 and 2 shipped: Agent::invite_details and
record::Invite now carry the parent room, so a front end CAN tell an
invite to a call from an invite to a chat. What it should DO with that
is open.

WHAT HAPPENS NOW, with a policy stricter than the default
invites = "any". A call is its own parent-dependent room and
Store::start_call invites the chat's people into it (decision
mimid-1wgh.113), so each of them gets a pending invite. On IRC,
Renderer::show_invites sends the user a raw INVITE to
names.invite_channel(&invite) -- a channel that does not exist and that
gets no channel even once joined (bead mimid-1wgh.114.6). The user
accepts and nothing appears to happen.

THE OPTIONS, as bead mimid-1wgh.130 framed them:

1. Accept a call's invite the way invites = "any" does, whatever the
   policy says. The argument: the call is already confined to the
   parent's people by room-policy-04 §5 and the hub enforces that, so
   the invite opens the user to nobody the chat has not already let in,
   and the policy's purpose is to stop strangers opening rooms. The
   argument against: a policy that says "never" meaning never is a
   policy the user set, and a call is still a room someone else made
   the user a member of.
2. Keep it pending but say what it is: the front end shows "a call in
   <chat>" rather than an invite to a room with no name. Honest, and it
   still asks a question the user may not be able to act on in time --
   a call is live for minutes.
3. Drop it: do not show a call's invite at all under a strict policy,
   and let the announcement of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 in the parent chat
   be the only thing the user sees. The call is then unjoinable for
   them, which is the status quo for a client with no VTC surface and
   is at least not confusing.

Whichever is chosen, IRC needs its own answer, because its INVITE
to a channel that will not exist is actively misleading, not merely
uninformative (bead mimid-1wgh.114.6 chose a NOTICE for the parallel
case of a keyed call starting elsewhere, which argues for option 2 or 3
here by consistency).

NOT URGENT. Nothing is visible with the default policy. It matters the
first time someone runs a stricter one.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"decision","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T16:32:28.222503728Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T16:32:28.222503728Z","labels":["human"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.114.16","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.114","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-25T16:32:28.261678567Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DECIDED by Mark 2026-11-25: join a call room's invite whatever the
invite policy says, and show no invite for it anywhere. Option 1.

So Store::sync's invite handling joins an invite whose
record::Invite::parent names a room this user is in, before the policy
is consulted, and no Change::InvitePending is recorded for it. The
announcement of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 in the parent chat stays the only
thing the user sees, which is what it was for.

WHY: a call room is confined to the parent chat's people by
room-policy-04 §5 and the hub enforces that at creation, so joining
admits nobody the chat has not already admitted. The invite policy
exists to stop strangers opening rooms, and this is not that. It also
makes calls work under a strict policy, where today they silently
cannot.

THE COST MARK ACCEPTED: a user who set invites = "never" meant never,
and this overrides them for one case. Narrowly: only for a room whose
parent they are already in, which room-policy §5 guarantees for a call.

This also removes the IRC trap of bead mimid-1wgh.114.6: no INVITE to a
channel that will never exist, because there is no invite.

NOT chosen: labelling the pending invite "a call in <chat>". Honest and
consistent with .114.6's NOTICE, but a call is live for minutes, so by
the time the user notices and accepts, it is over -- truthful about
something they cannot act on.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: the parent check must be "a room this user is in",
not merely "parent is Some". A call room whose parent this agent does
not hold would otherwise be auto-joined on a peer's word."}
